errors: The first solver clamped emitter backflow inside the Newton step, which broke mass balance by up to 73 gpm on two networks while still reporting convergence. The EPANET comparison and the mass-balance test caught it, and check-valve status switching fixed it.
EPANET's toolkit wrote a binary scratch file into the venture directory and it got committed. It was removed in the next commit, and epanet_compare.py now writes it to the temp dir.
wntr 1.5.0 needed 'six' installed by hand; toolkit.EN_PRESSURE does not exist, so the EPANET enum codes were used directly.

doc_friction.issue: It stops at the first failing stage, so a too-long post description and then a too-long seo_title took two extra 5-minute reruns. Checking post front matter before the site tests, or reporting every stage's failures together, would have saved that.

notes: Explore idea: sprinkler-hydraulic-calc, fire sprinkler hydraulics for tree, loop and grid systems by the global gradient algorithm (EPANET's method), with heads as emitters that shut like check valves. Verified against EPANET 2.2 (wntr 1.5.0 toolkit) on 59 of 61 seeded networks to 4.6e-7 psi / 1.4e-6 gpm. A branch line matches the hand method to 1e-6 psi. Finding: at the same pipe sizes, a 10-line grid with the design area at the far end needs 18-68% less source pressure than a tree. Checks: run_venture_tests (sprinkler-hydraulic-calc, water-supply-sizing) ok; venture-preflight clean including the full build; Chromium at 1280/390 px with no console errors. Not checked against a real designer's calculation.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: an engineer building and verifying a gradient network solver, page and EPANET harness: about three days

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
